description: A clear sizing solution made by dissolving isinglass or good gelatine in water, used warm to re-strengthen weakened paper and to carry staining colour. Cockerell notes that quality matters: pure gelatine yields a clear, odourless solution, while impure stock smells foul and turns gluey.
name: gelatine size

source_ref.label: Douglas Cockerell, Bookbinding and the Care of Books (D. Appleton, 1901), Internet Archive
